topStory.text: NVIDIA's Q2 FY27: revenue $96.2B, up 106% year over year, with data-center revenue of $89.0B (+117% YoY, +18% sequentially) and Q3 guided to $108B — guidance that assumes no data-center compute revenue from China. Jensen Huang: 'AI has reached its inflection point... compute is revenue. And demand is accelerating.' The quarter caps an earnings season in which Amazon, Alphabet and Meta all raised 2026 capex, lifting the tracked operator run-rate to ~$877B.

feed.text: Q2 earnings reset the 2026 capex baseline: Amazon lifted guidance to $220B citing higher memory costs and warned it still won't have enough capacity to meet demand; Alphabet raised to $195–205B on faster capacity delivery; Meta lifted its floor to $130–145B as the buildout consumed nearly all quarterly operating cash flow. This dashboard's tracked operator capex moves from ~$839B to ~$877B.

Micron unveiled Micron Research Labs in Boise — a $10B, decade-long commitment to a dedicated US memory-research hub covering advanced memory and compute architectures, packaging and future manufacturing, with construction starting 2027. It sits on top of the $250B+ Micron has already committed to US manufacturing and R&D as the HBM crunch keeps pacing accelerator output.

TerraPower says its next Natrium plant — the first aimed at a data center, customer still undisclosed — will be announced this year and break ground in 2027. The 345 MW molten-salt design stores excess heat and taps it to boost output when demand spikes, the pitch for AI loads; Meta agreed in January to buy eight Natrium plants. Advanced nuclear stays the longest path to firm power, but it is now signing commercial customers.

Dell'Oro Group nearly doubled its 2030 outlook in eight months: worldwide data-center capex is now forecast to surpass $3 trillion by 2030, up from its January 2026 view, on higher hyperscaler guidance, bigger global power-capacity projections and rising commodity costs. High-end AI accelerators remain the largest single line and the primary growth driver, while the new AI-specialized cloud segment (model builders and neoclouds) grows at nearly a 60% CAGR. Dell'Oro notes the top four US hyperscalers alone could be about half of global capex — capital is scaling faster than the power to deploy it.

Bloomberg's analysis of BloombergNEF data counts 99 proposed on-site natural-gas plants — about 126 GW across 22 states, more than a third of it in Texas — being built to power US data centers. Run at industry-standard rates they would emit roughly 318 million metric tons of CO2 a year, lifting US power-sector emissions about 20%, and up to a third if run flat out. Amazon's Pecos County, Texas site and Microsoft's West Texas complex behind a Chevron-built plant account for more than 10 GW and up to 45 Mt CO2e between them.

NVIDIA's 8-K discloses residual value guaranties backstopping OpenAI's leases at SB Energy's PORTS Technology Campus in Pike County, Ohio — roughly 4.25 GW of IT load, with NVIDIA's aggregate payment obligation cumulatively capped at $105B and discretion to add credit support for about 3.8 GW more. If OpenAI defaults or becomes insolvent, NVIDIA pays the shortfall between each lease's guaranteed minimum value and what a replacement lease or sale recovers; the obligation lapses once OpenAI achieves a satisfactory credit rating, and OpenAI has agreed to reimburse NVIDIA for any amount it actually pays. Leases are expected to reach ready-for-service beginning in 2028. The chip supplier is now underwriting its largest customer's real estate.

The 60-day deadline arrived for all six FERC-jurisdictional RTOs/ISOs — PJM, MISO, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE and CAISO — to answer FERC's June 18 show-cause orders, which preliminarily found their large-load interconnection rules may be 'unjust, unreasonable or unduly discriminatory.' Each had to justify its existing tariff or propose reforms for connecting loads of 50 MW or more at 69 kV and above. Interested parties now get 30 days to respond to those filings, closing the comment window around Sep 16.

PJM formally filed its large-load framework at FERC in docket ER26-3515, requesting an Oct 12, 2026 effective date. Any site adding 50 MW or more of cumulative peak demand after June 1, 2027 must designate qualifying new capacity at least equal to its peak, and any unsupported portion is curtailed ahead of pre-emergency demand response — exposure a load can reduce or eliminate through the 'bring your own new capacity' (BYONC) path. PJM's case for it: roughly 70 GW of new large load projected by 2038 against about 15 GW of generation retired since 2022.

feed.text: Rep. Andrea Salinas (D-Ore.) introduced the Data Center Community Reinvestment Act of 2026 (H.R. 10102), which would levy a federal excise tax of 1 cent per kilowatt-hour on electricity used by data centers above 1 MW of maximum rated capacity or peak load, raising an estimated $1.76B a year split evenly across the Land and Water Conservation Fund, Housing Trust Fund, Superfund, Highway Trust Fund and a new energy-technology fund. It was referred to Ways and Means with no clear path to passage; critics note a flat consumption tax does not distinguish between loads by their actual grid impact.

More than two-thirds of the electricity sought for US AI data centers is unlikely to ever materialize, per new Wood Mackenzie projections: grid operators and utilities will likely commit to only about 28% of the 1,066 GW currently requested nationwide, with the rest 'phantom' — duplicative or non-binding requests filed at multiple utilities simultaneously with no realistic path to construction.

NVIDIA signed MOUs with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to establish financing platforms mobilizing more than $500B of third-party capital for AI infrastructure — structured so outside investors fund data centers and power for NVIDIA's own customers (frontier labs, enterprises, AI clouds) without loading its balance sheet, with NVIDIA compute itself treated as the investable collateral. Subject to final agreements.

HD Hyundai Heavy Industries secured a $675M deal — its largest-ever power-engine order — to supply 1,000 MW of HiMSEN gas-engine generating capacity to a US data center project via developer Coban Energy Group, underscoring how quickly demand for on-site/behind-the-meter generation equipment is scaling.
